newsitem.title: USA: SEC probe of Centennial Tech continuing-records.
newsitem.headline: SEC probe of Centennial Tech continuing-records.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into Centennial Technologies Inc and its ex-CEO is continuing, according to federal court documents.

In an affadavit filed with the U.S. District Court in Boston, the SEC said it began investigating the Billerica, Mass.-based computer card maker in January, before the company issued what it now concedes to be overstated earnings and revenues for the second quarter of 1997.
The company sacked its founder and Chief Executive Officer Emanuel Pinez February 11.
Pinez, a 58-year-old Israeli citizen, remained in a federal jail on charges of insider trading and securities fraud Friday.

Separately, U.S. District Judge Patti Sarris agreed to modify a temporary restraining order that froze Pinez's assets to allow both Lehman Bros Holdings Inc and PaineWebber Group Inc to liquidate enough of his accounts to settle an estimated $21 million debt.

Under Sarris's order, the two brokerage firms can liquidate both Centennial stock and options in Pinez's account but must keep the funds in two separate escrow accounts at least until a hearing set for Monday afternoon.

The SEC affadavit into the alleged "ongoing fraud" estimates that Pinez's profit from 2,400 call options, which he bought between Feb 7 and Feb 10, could have net him a profit of $447,500 and Pinez stood to gain "substantially more" from his purchase of 1,955 puts.

At the time, however, the New York Stock Exchange had halted trading in the stock before Pinez could exercise those options. The stock closed at 16-1/2 on Feb 10. Trading has since resumed and in early afternoon activity, Centennial was trading at 2-1/4. The Exchange has said it will move to de-list the stock as of March 3.

According to the court papers, the SEC is aware that Pinez held accounts at Oppenheimer and Co, Hambrecht & Quist Group Inc and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette as well as accounts at two foreign banks and about six U.S-based banks, but it is still trying to ascertain if there are other accounts and assets.
